page: Amazon Web Services i7i.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors delivering 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs clocked at 3.2 GHz, backed by 320 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 running at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. For high-throughput local operations, the server integrates 22,500 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 56 Gbps. The architecture omits dedicated GPUs, focusing strictly on high-density compute, expansive memory, and direct-attached storage performance.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded execution and storage-adjacent computation. The instance scores 22,370.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 95,121.66 in the PassMark CPU suite, both landing in the top tier of evaluated hardware. Memory subsystems achieve strong throughput, recording 289.55 GB/s in large-block uncached read operations and 6,647.86 GB/s for small-block cached reads. In real-world data processing metrics, the system delivers 33,628.93 points in PassMark database operations and sustained 122.39 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, accompanied by static web serving throughput of 136.82 GB/s.

Because the server combines bare-metal hardware access with massive NVMe SSD density and high memory bandwidth, it provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for resource-heavy workloads that saturate IOPS and memory channels. The primary tradeoff is the fixed allocation of substantial local storage and compute, which can introduce resource underutilization if tasks do not require continuous high-speed disk access or 96 vCPUs. AWS i7i.metal-24xl is best suited for large-scale transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching systems, and high-concurrency data ingestion pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.metal-24xl is a bare-metal storage-optimized instance engineered for data-intensive enterprise workloads. Equipped with dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors on the x86_64 architecture, it features 48 physical cores, 96 vCPUs running at 3.2 GHz, and 320 MB of L3 cache. The platform includes 768.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory alongside 22,500 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and 56 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without discrete GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier results in PassMark database operations and multi-core CPU metrics, alongside strong Redis throughput reaching 122.39 million operations per second. By combining direct hardware access with substantial fast storage and high memory bandwidth, it offers strong qualitative efficiency for IOPS-critical applications. It is tailored for large-scale transactional databases, distributed NoSQL clusters, real-time analytics, and high-throughput data processing engines.
